analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלֶּה means “these three.” The following בְּנֵי נֹחַ identifies the three as Noah’s sons.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral, used with the masculine plural בְּנֵי.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67081:0, 66052:0.
analysis.morphology: Common plural demonstrative pronoun without a prefix or suffix.

draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי נֹחַ, “these three are the sons of Noah,” the name completes the construct phrase בְּנֵי נֹחַ and identifies the father of the three.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי נֹחַ identifies ‘these three’ as Noah’s sons. וּמֵאֵלֶּה repeats the demonstrative with ‘from’, identifying the three sons as the source from whom the earth’s population spread.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means ‘and’. The prefixed preposition מֵ is a form of מִן ‘from’. אֵלֶּה is a common-gender plural demonstrative pronoun.

analysis.evidence: וּמֵאֵלֶּה means “and from these,” referring to Noah’s three sons. כָל הָאָרֶץ denotes the earth’s population, which spread out from them.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person feminine singular, agreeing with the feminine singular הָאָרֶץ in כָל הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: כָל הָאָרֶץ means “the whole earth.” The verse traces its entire population back to Noah’s three sons.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, followed by הָאָרֶץ.
